solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What'll we see serge in? Our recommendation has mark of correctness

blocks.note: the Chambers Dictionary is the reference Azed recommends to solvers
a tick marks an answer as right

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where to look up the cloth serge, and a teacher ticks the recommended dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a CHAMBERSTICK holds the candle by whose light we would see a serge garment in a bedroom at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamberstick is a short candlestick with a handle, carried to light the way to bed, so things are seen by its candle.

clue.text: School's dep. sacked where union holds sway (10, two words)

indicators.note: something sacked is ransacked and thrown about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: every letter of the two words, apostrophe and full stop ignored

explanation.surface: A school's deputy head is fired at a workplace where the teaching union has the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace where every employee must belong to a trade union, so the union is dominant there.

clue.text: Like beefcake in thick pieces without cold topping

indicators.note: the topping is the first letter, and the cold one is to be done without, so the leading letter goes

blocks.note: food in thick pieces is chunky

explanation.surface: A beefcake model is described as if he were stewing steak cut thick and served without a cold garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the usual abbreviation for cold, here sitting conveniently at the top of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefcake is slang for muscular, attractive men, and hunky describes exactly that kind of sturdy good-looking build.

clue.text: Member of sect? I'll get involved in second one

indicators.note: to get involved in something is to end up inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written
the letter I, the subject of 'will get involved'

explanation.surface: A recruit to a sect admits they will join in at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moonie is a follower of the Unification Church founded by Sun Myung Moon, often called a sect.

clue.text: Book penned in a thorny tree? An ill- conceived idea

indicators.note: something penned in is shut inside an enclosure, so one letter sits within the tree's name

blocks.note: B is a standard abbreviation for book
the bael is a thorny Indian tree, the Bengal quince

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of keeping a book inside a spiky tree, and admits it was a daft notion.
explanation.walkthrough: The bael sits in Chambers; the B is placed after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives babel as a visionary or ill-conceived plan, after the Tower of Babel whose builders aimed to reach heaven.

clue.text: Hut for travellers rest, last given precedence

indicators.note: the final letter is allowed to go ahead of all the others, moving round to the front

blocks.note: an anchor is something that holds steady, a support or rest

explanation.surface: A wayside shelter for travellers offers rest, with the last to arrive served first.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers defines a rancho as a hut or group of huts put up for travellers, from Spanish for a mess or camp.

clue.text: Jock's rattled, with bonds round both hands

indicators.note: the bonds go round, enclosing what comes after them

blocks.note: bonds as a verb, ties up
R and L, right and left hands

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is shaken up after being tied at both wrists.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is crossword shorthand for a Scot, marking a Scots word; 'bonds' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To tirl is a Scots verb meaning to rattle, especially a door latch, so tirled is its past tense.

clue.text: Having completed MA, I had about abandoned pen etc

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order
about means around, so the first word's letters surround the others

blocks.note: I'd is the short form of I had
all six letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A new master's graduate gives up writing with pen and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge to incept was formally to take a master's or doctor's degree, so having incepted means having done so.

clue.text: Devilish villainess gang once completely overturned

indicators.note: turning over a word in a down light flips its letter order

blocks.note: crue is an obsolete spelling of crew, a gang
all, as in all done

explanation.surface: A gang of villains is entirely defeated by a fiendish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devilish' is a nod to her surname, de Vil.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruella de Vil is the wicked woman in The Hundred and One Dalmatians who wants puppies for a fur coat.

clue.text: Ivy follows line that's contested on the board

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
udo is a Japanese plant of the ivy family, eaten as a vegetable

explanation.surface: Ivy grows behind a line of contested ground in a boardroom battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts the ivy after the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple dice game in which players race their counters round a board against one another.

clue.text: Some banks charging extras? A racket

definitions.note: plural: the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: charging here means loading or carrying, so the following words hold the letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A complaint that some banks charging for extras are running a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like the money kind; it means ridges of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Asar is the plural of as, an esker: a long glacial ridge of gravel, a kind of bank.

clue.text: Southern borough the Scots plundered

blocks.note: S for southern
a borough is a town

explanation.surface: A town in the south of Britain was looted by raiders from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scots' is not the raiders but a label: the word is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stown is the Scots past participle of steal, so it means stolen or plundered.

clue.text: What Japanese rarely dressed without – or is this for ferry?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about whether some item is meant for a ferry crossing
setter's reading: the letters O and R stand inside the abbreviation for a roll-on roll-off ferry, and the answer, split into two words, says just where they are

explanation.surface: A traditional Japanese accessory is mentioned, then someone asks whether it is meant for the ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: RO-RO is the roll-on roll-off ferry; the answer can be read as IN RO, so 'OR is IN RO(-RO)'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inro is a small lacquered box for seals and medicines hung from the sash of traditional Japanese dress.

clue.text: Unwelcome comforters called this 'doing normal work'

blocks.note: first meaning: Job's comforters called ..., visiting him in his suffering
second meaning: at work, as in on the job

explanation.walkthrough: Job's comforters are friends who make things worse; in the Bible they came to visit the afflicted Job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means visiting the biblical sufferer, and also at one's ordinary labour, as on the job.

clue.text: Ocular deposit? Old poet, I'll be seen with this, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words might be rearranged into the opening phrase of the clue

blocks.note: the seven letters as written
the letter I, subject of 'will be seen'
'this' stands for the answer itself, added to the mix

explanation.surface: An elderly poet expects to be spotted with a growth in his eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: OLD POET plus I plus the answer ('this') rearrange to OCULAR DEPOSIT, so the answer is what is left of those letters once OLD POET and I are taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcus senilis is a greyish ring of fatty deposit round the cornea, common in older people.

clue.text: Peg ropes on board ship, showing stamina

indicators.note: goods on board a vessel are carried inside it

blocks.note: a tee is the golfer's peg
on a ship ropes are lines
SS for steamship

explanation.surface: Sailors pegging out ropes aboard ship show their staying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeliness is hardness and resolve, an unyielding toughness close in sense to staying power.

clue.text: Knife, even used in cracking cockles

indicators.note: cracking breaks things open, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: ene is an old form of even, as evening
all seven letters

explanation.surface: A knife is needed, even so, for prising open shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' means the archaic word, not 'level'; its letters go in with the shellfish before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A skene-occle is a Highland dagger tucked in the sleeve, related to the skean-dhu worn in the stocking.

clue.text: Pay o? bit left in a payment due to new ruler

definitions.note: the source has lost the ff ligature: it reads Pay off

indicators.note: in places the first item within the second

blocks.note: an ort is a scrap of food left over

blocks.clueFragment: a payment due to new ruler
blocks.note: a, plus mise: a payment made to a new king or lord on accession

explanation.surface: Someone pays off, a little at a time, the levy owed to a new monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The source's 'Pay o?' is 'Pay off' with its ff ligature lost. Mise is an old word for a payment to a new ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise a debt is to pay it off by regular instalments over time.

clue.text: Scots pipe was reeling, mostly round piano

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
round means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps the next letter

blocks.note: to reel is to wheel or spin round
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A Scottish piper staggered drunkenly round a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' is a verb, to whistle, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheeple is a Scots verb meaning to whistle feebly, like a bird's thin call, so to pipe.

clue.text: Behaviour of Trump men adore, abnormally

indicators.note: abnormally means not in the usual way, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

blocks.note: all eight letters

explanation.surface: A comment on how a president's conduct wins the unusual adoration of his male fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Trump' signals the American spelling, without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanor is the US spelling of demeanour, a person's outward conduct or bearing.

clue.text: Norman going after English? He sends unwritten message

blocks.note: E for English
Norman Mailer, the American novelist

explanation.surface: Norman follows English? as if a writer were pursuing a nationality, with a puzzle about a message nobody wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like the medieval invaders; it is the writer Norman Mailer, placed after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emailer sends electronic messages, which are typed rather than written by hand on paper.

clue.text: Drink up, a drink (not grand) imbibed? They could be grand

indicators.note: in a down light, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
G is the slang grand, a thousand, and not means it is taken away
something imbibed is drunk and so ends up inside

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink
taken as written
nog is a strong ale or egg drink

explanation.surface: Down a drink, not an expensive one, someone urges, while reflecting that it could be grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' plays two parts: G (a thousand pounds) to remove, and the grand piano in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianos come as uprights or grands, so a grand is one possible kind of piano.

clue.text: What, digging into pot, my very tight clothes do, bit by bit

indicators.note: this is a reverse clue: the answer digs into the next word to make a phrase, so the solver takes that word's letters back out of the phrase

blocks.note: taken as written; its P and OT are wrapped round the answer
what very tight clothes do: pinch me a lot

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their snug outfit squeezes into their pot belly, little by little.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: put the answer into POT and you get P-INCHMEAL-OT, read as 'pinch me a lot', which is what very tight clothes do.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchmeal is an old adverb meaning gradually, by inches at a time.

clue.text: Write a score part for one of the foregoing? Ta – terriffc

indicators.note: part means only a portion of each item is used, the end of one and the start of the others

blocks.note: the foregoing is the answer at 21 down, so one of them is a single piano; its last two letters are kept
taken as written
only the first two letters are kept

explanation.surface: A composer is thanked for writing a score for an instrument, with an enthusiastic 'terrific'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the foregoing' points back to 21 down: one piano. The source's 'terriffc' is 'terrific' with a ligature mangled.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate music is to write it down in a score using musical notation.

clue.text: Part of marine organism, catch hauled up devoured by odd members of crew

indicators.note: hauled up in a down light means drawn upwards, so read from the bottom
the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are the ones kept
what is devoured ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: to net is to catch
first and third letters

explanation.surface: Fishermen haul up a catch and a sea creature is eaten by part of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A ctene is one of the comb-like swimming plates on a comb jelly, so it is a part of that sea creature.

clue.text: Half of Panama let off It's to do with canal's opening

definitions.text: It's to do with canal's opening

indicators.note: half of a word means only three of its six letters stay
off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the back half is kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: Half of Panama is closed off, which concerns the opening of its famous canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' looks like the Panama Canal; it is a body passage, whose opening is a meatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatal is the adjective from meatus, the anatomical name for the opening of a duct or passage.

clue.text: A grain, mostly included in heated meat stew with veg, …

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used
included in places these letters inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
rice is a cereal grain
heated things are hot

explanation.surface: A cook adds a little grain to a hot stew of meat and vegetables, with more to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads on to the next clue, which names the dessert served after this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot, also haricot mutton, is a ragout of mutton with beans or turnips, a meaty vegetable stew.

clue.text: Had onset of niggle in insides, laid up

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter is used
in places that letter inside the next word
laid up in a down light means set upwards, so read from bottom to top

blocks.note: guts are innards
first letter

explanation.surface: Someone was off sick with a nagging pain in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' is the definition, in the sense of conned.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had is to be cheated, and stung is slang for overcharged or swindled.

clue.text: Topper collapsing, second in line, with nasty bugs around

indicators.note: nasty suggests something gone bad and twisted out of shape
second in a word picks out its second letter
around places the first set of letters about the selected one

blocks.note: all four letters
second letter

explanation.surface: A top hat falls apart while lined up second, with nasty insects all round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibus is an opera hat, a top hat with a spring so that it folds flat.

clue.text: … Followed by this treat cooked by Jacques, new? (10, two words)

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: all five letters
Jacques Tati, the French film comedian
N for new

explanation.surface: Continuing the meal from the previous clue: a dessert made by a French chef follows the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition picks up from 26 across: the stew is followed by this pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarte Tatin is an upside-down caramelised apple tart, a French dessert that would follow a main course.

clue.text: Pizzicato sound, soft, part of chain

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
a link is one part of a chain

explanation.surface: A quietly plucked note is described as one link in a chain of sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Plink imitates the short, light sound of a plucked string, which is what pizzicato playing produces.

clue.text: Basin replacing bend in use for piping that's far from straight

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes another's place in the word

blocks.note: a tub is a basin
an S-bend is the curved trap in plumbing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber swaps a washbasin for the bend when fitting crooked pipework.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-tube is a tube bent into a U shape, so it is piping that is anything but straight.

clue.text: Monetary unit in Peru and so on

blocks.note: PE is Peru's international country code
taken as written

explanation.surface: A currency used in Peru and similar countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and so on' reads as a set phrase, but 'so' is placed on PE.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency of several Latin American countries, such as Mexico, Chile and Colombia.

clue.text: US secretary with no love for deadly piece

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so that item is removed

blocks.note: steno is American for a stenographer
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: An American secretary with no romantic attachments is a dangerous character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is slang for a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War, and a piece is slang for a gun.

clue.text: Mean muse that's shunned this writer twice – waste passage ends here

indicators.note: shunned means avoided, so those letters are kept out of the phrase

blocks.note: the two words run together
this writer is the setter, me, taken twice

explanation.surface: A miserly muse has turned her back on the poet twice, and inspiration has run into the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: One ME is taken from the start of 'mean'; the other's M and E come from 'muse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The anus is the opening at the end of the gut, where waste leaves the body.

clue.text: Urged girl to accept good moulded fragile stuff (12, two words)

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: pressed means urged
a lass is a girl
G for good

explanation.surface: A girl was urged to take good care of a delicate moulded ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed glass is shaped by pressing molten glass into a mould, and glass is a brittle material.
